parsed.explanation: Combined regime pairs a documented federal tier-1 exposure—binary passport processing, entry officers instructed to refuse on document discrepancy and consider permanent ineligibility, and birth-sex federal facilities—with a strongly protective state regime on care, discrimination and hate crime. Adult alone has no documented likely imprisonment or execution, but outing at entry can cause refusal/stranding and, if detained federally, hormone removal and reported custody abuse. For minors/families, the state shield protects against other-state process while federal care/school investigations remain a competing exposure. State protections do not cancel federal screening, facilities or custody.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary sex definition; X-marker passports stopped Feb 2025, Supreme Court allowed restrictions Nov 2025; passports confiscated/blocked and travellers stranded; cable directs refusal on discrepancy and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, not automatic, limited waivers exist; ACLU suit pending. State licence X/no-documentation is resident-facing and not a visitor entry protection.
entry_documents.interaction: Home-passport marker/presentation mismatch at national entry occurs before state protections apply; state ID openness does not cure federal refusal or lifetime-ineligibility risk.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections from 2026: conversion-therapy practices, short haircuts, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution; stopped reporting trans prisoners. Immigration custody: reported forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. Civil-liberties litigation is pending and some federal orders enjoined, but no documented visitor remedy in custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry discrepancy or other detention can transfer visitor into federal custody where birth-sex placement, care denial and abuse are documented; state anti-discrimination law does not govern federal custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with gender identity. Nationally 9+1 jurisdictions ban in all government buildings, 9 more partially, 3 schools-only; 4 criminalise some use, with a documented trespass arrest (60 days, 24h men's ward) in another jurisdiction.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State prohibits gender-identity discrimination in public accommodations since 1993 and repealed exclusions in 2023; this division is in most-protective tier, so no state bathroom ban is documented for it.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State public-accommodation protection remains subject to federal-building rules for federal facilities; state ban status for this division is not_documented in the mapped groups.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders characterise minors' gender-affirming care as mutilation, freeze funding, propose barring public insurance under 18, subpoena hospital records for under-19 patients; some orders blocked/enjoined, status unresolved.
care_services.protection: State 2023 shield law declares other jurisdictions' care laws against public policy, bars out-of-state subpoenas, warrants, extradition and custody removal for legal care; public insurance covers trans care and insurers may not exclude it.
care_services.interaction: Shield protects travelling families from other-state process and secures state care access, but does not document immunity from federal investigation, funding or subpoena power.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy prioritises groups described as radically pro-transgender; justice guidance uses radical gender ideology framing and creates cash rewards for terrorist-leadership tips, though never as a standalone criterion.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State hate-crime penalties for gender identity since 1993, trans-panic defence abolished 2024, anti-discrimination law since 1993; national hate-crime statute also covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal threat-framing increases outing and investigation risk nationally, while state law provides hate-crime and civil recourse only within state jurisdiction.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal orders direct investigation of schools for gender ideology and criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; women's sports entry ban; proposed care reimbursement bars; hospital record subpoenas for minors.
minors_guardians.protection: State shield bars other-state custody removal or warrants over legal care and protects travelling families; conversion therapy banned for minors/vulnerable adults; care is covered and affirmatively protected.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor may access state-protected care yet face federal school, sports, funding or records exposure; guardian/provider liability is traveller-facing for families.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific trans-violence figure is documented; absence is not safety. Federal immigration-custody abuse is documented, and national public opinion in 2025 showed 66% support for birth-sex document laws.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime enhancements, long-standing anti-discrimination law and most-protective independent tier indicate institutional protection; enforcement complaints/outcomes are not sourced.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street-level state recourse may operate, but federal custody abuse and federal facility/entry enforcement are outside that recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport and executive-order litigation unresolved; Supreme Court allowed passport restriction; several orders enjoined but practical effect depends on timing of travel.
remedies_unknowns.protection: State courts, anti-discrimination and hate-crime provisions, legal-aid FAQ and shield law are documented protections, though shield has no documented decided visitor cases and enforcement data are not sourced.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are slow, split by sovereign and stage: state relief does not reliably stop federal entry refusal, federal facilities or federal custody practices.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than this jurisdiction: that anchor combines birth-sex prison housing with assaults and a criminal cross-dressing arrest power. Here adult imprisonment for identity is not documented, and state protections are stronger, though federal custody abuse keeps severity high if detained.

Similar: extended screening, humiliation, possible administrative refusal/return, slow remedies and officer discretion, without credible execution. This case adds federal facility exclusion and documented custody care-denial, but state shield/anti-discrimination offsets bring it near this level.

Higher than this jurisdiction: that anchor has explicit equality coverage, respectful border practice, independent oversight and compensatory remedies after incidents. Here federal passport/entry and facility rules are themselves restrictive and litigation is unresolved, preventing a low-risk rating.

parsed.synthesis: The operative sequence is federal-first: passport/entry screening can refuse or strand a visitor before state protections operate; federal facilities apply birth-sex rules inside federal buildings; detention can lead to documented hormone removal and custody abuse. The state materially mitigates local life—shielded care for travelling families, anti-discrimination and hate-crime law, no documented state bathroom ban—and prevents a 0.35-level rating. Because those protections do not cancel federal entry, facility or custody exposures and their visitor enforcement is undocumented, the combined regime sits near the administrative-exclusion anchors rather than the protected anchors.
